## Biological Narrative

The RaMP enrichment analysis identifies **Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG map00260)** as the top affected pathway, with a fold-enrichment of 568.9 (FDR = 0.0) across matched input metabolites. A second strongly supported candidate is **Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives (Reactome R-HSA-71291)**, which shares most of the same drivers and reflects broader amino-group metabolism disruption.

The enrichment pattern converges on the **methionine cycle** as a central hub. L-methionine (C00073) is confirmed upstream of S-adenosylhomocysteine (C00021) via S-adenosylmethionine (C00019) in just two KEGG reaction steps, establishing a clear directional relationship. L-cysteine (C00097) connects to S-adenosylhomocysteine through a longer path. Ornithine (C00077) and 2-ketobutyric acid (C00109) are matched members of the glycine, serine and threonine metabolism pathway alongside the methionine-cycle intermediates.

In biological terms, the coordinated elevation of these metabolites is consistent with perturbation of **Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG map00260)** and its associated amino-acid network. S-adenosylhomocysteine is a direct by-product of methyltransferase reactions; elevated levels can inhibit S-adenosylmethionine–dependent methyltransferases, broadly suppressing methylation capacity. Lipoic acid (C16241) participates as an essential cofactor in oxidative decarboxylation reactions within this metabolic zone. Phenylephrine (C07441) and nitrate (C00244) were also detected.

Collectively, the data are most consistent with **altered methyl-group availability and amino-acid flux** in the treatment group, with L-methionine and S-adenosylhomocysteine serving as primary drivers anchored in Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism.

**Limitations:** The enrichment results cover only metabolites with KEGG annotations that map to the curated RaMP database; the four remaining input compounds were not represented in the top pathways and could not be connected directionally.
